events.text: Diocletian and  Maximian retired as co-rulers of the Roman Empire, being succeeded by Galerius and Constantius Chlorus.
A synod in Carthage condemns Pelagianism.

main.desc: 3rd–5th century church synods held in Africa

events.text: The Nea Ekklesia church in Constantinople, on which many later cross-in-square Eastern Orthodox churches were based, was consecrated.

main.desc: Byzantine church in Constantinople (now Istanbul) from 880 to 1490

events.text: Norman mercenaries landed at Bannow Bay in Leinster, beginning the Norman invasion of Ireland.
Norman mercenaries land at Bannow Bay in Leinster, marking the beginning of the Norman invasion of Ireland.
Wars of Scottish Independence end: By the Treaty of Edinburgh–Northampton, England recognises Scotland as an independent state.

main.desc: War of national liberation between Scotland and England

events.text: Scottish Royal forces loyal to King James II defeat a rebel army of the Black Douglases in the battle of Arkinholm.
The Edict of Expulsion is officially proclaimed in Castile, requiring all Jewish residents to leave within three months.
Stephen Báthory and Anna Jagiellon  were crowned as the elected rulers of the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth.

main.desc: Ruler of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth from 1576 to 1586

events.text: Dutch–Portuguese War: Portuguese and Spanish forces recaptured the Brazilian city of Bahia, which had previously been captured by the Dutch Republic.
Henry Morgan's raid on Lake Maracaibo: the Spanish Armada de Barlovento is defeated by an English Privateer fleet led by Captain Henry Morgan.

main.t: Henry Morgan's raid on Lake Maracaibo

events.text: Francis Nicholson and James Blair organize five May Day orations given by students of the College of William & Mary, leading to the establishment of Williamsburg as Virginia's new capital.
Under the terms of the Acts of Union, the Kingdoms of England and Scotland merged to form the Kingdom of Great Britain, with a single parliament and government based in Westminster.

main.desc: Acts of Parliament creating the Kingdom of Great Britain

events.text: The Act of Union joining England and Scotland to form the Kingdom of Great Britain takes effect.

main.desc: Acts of Parliament creating the Kingdom of Great Britain

events.text: Publication of Species Plantarum by Linnaeus, and the formal start date of plant taxonomy adopted by the International Code of Botanical Nomenclature.

links.t: International Code of Nomenclature for algae, fungi, and plants

events.text: The Marriage of Figaro (audio featured), an opera buffa by Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart, premiered at the Burgtheater in Vienna.
War of the Pyrenees: France regained nearly all the land it lost to Spain the previous year with its victory in the Second Battle of Boulou.

main.desc: 1793–95 French Revolutionary war against Spain and Portugal

events.text: The Slave Trade Act 1807 takes effect, abolishing the slave trade within the British Empire.

main.desc: Act of the Parliament of the United Kingdom

events.text: Execution of the Cato Street Conspirators, who plotted to kill the British Cabinet and Prime Minister Lord Liverpool.

main.desc: 1820 planned assassination attempt on UK Government ministers

events.text: Queen Victoria opens The Great Exhibition at The Crystal Palace in London.

main.desc: Queen of the United Kingdom from 1837 to 1901

events.text: American Civil War: The Battle of Chancellorsville between Robert E. Lee's Confederate Army of Northern Virginia and the Union Army of the Potomac under Joseph Hooker begins.
American Civil War: During the Vicksburg campaign, Union forces under Ulysses S. Grant win the Battle of Port Gibson and establish a firm presence on the east side of the Mississippi River.

main.desc: Military campaign of the American Civil War

events.text: The Empire of Brazil, Argentina, and Uruguay sign the Treaty of the Triple Alliance.
The Memphis Race Riots begin. Over three days, 46 blacks and two whites were killed. Reports of the atrocities influenced passage of the Fourteenth Amendment to the United States Constitution.

main.desc: Massacre of the Black community of Memphis, Tennessee

links.t: Fourteenth Amendment to the United States Constitution

events.text: Moses Fleetwood Walker (pictured), the last African American in Major League Baseball until Jackie Robinson, played his first game for the Toledo Blue Stockings.
The original Chicago Board of Trade Building opened for business.

Rallies are held throughout the United States demanding the eight-hour work day, culminating in the Haymarket affair in Chicago, in commemoration of which May 1 is celebrated as International Workers' Day in many countries.
The 1891 New Orleans Lynchings: 11 Italian immigrants are lynched by a mob in Louisiana, USA after the acquittal of several defendants in a murder case, the largest mass lynching in U.S. history.

main.desc: Murder of eleven Italian men by a mob

events.text: On Labor Day in Catania, Sicily, workers establish the first successful Fascio Siciliano, launching a movement of peasants and laborers protesting poverty, landlordism, taxation, and economic hardship across Sicily.

main.desc: Federal holiday in the United States

events.text: Coxey's Army, the first significant American protest march, arrives in Washington, D.C.
While on a pilgrimage of Shah Abdol-Azim Shrine in Ray, Tehran, Naser al-Din Shah of Qajar Persia, was assassinated by Mirza Reza Kermani.

main.desc: Mosque and mausoleum complex in Rey, Tehran, Iran

events.text: The Ramakrishna Mission was founded by Swami Vivekananda to serve as the humanitarian counterpart to the Hindu monastic order Ramakrishna Math.

Spanish–American War: Battle of Manila Bay: The Asiatic Squadron of the United States Navy destroys the Pacific Squadron of the Spanish Navy after a seven-hour battle. Spain loses all seven of its ships, and 381 Spanish sailors die. There are no American vessel losses or combat deaths.

main.desc: 1898 conflict between Spain and the United States

events.text: A dust explosion at a coal mine near Scofield, Utah, U.S., killed at least 200 miners.

main.desc: Rapid combustion of fine particles suspended in the air

events.text: The Scofield Mine disaster kills over 200 men in Scofield, Utah in what is to date the fifth-worst mining accident in United States history.

main.desc: 1900 explosion of a coal mine in Utah

events.text: The Jaffa riots begin.
The 7.2 Mw Kopet Dag earthquake shakes the Iran–Turkmenistan border region with a maximum Mercalli intensity of IX (Violent), killing up to 3,800 and injuring 1,121.

main.desc: Earthquake centered on the Iran-Turkmenistan border

events.text: New York City's Empire State Building (pictured), at the time the tallest building in the world, opened.

main.desc: Office skyscraper in Manhattan, New York

links.t: History of the world's tallest structures

events.text: Citizen Kane, a widely acclaimed film by actor and director Orson Welles, premiered.

links.t: List of films voted the best

events.text: Second World War: British and Indian forces conducted a successful airborne assault on a Japanese artillery battery during the advance to liberate Rangoon, Burma.

World War II: German radio broadcasts news of Adolf Hitler's death, falsely stating that he has "fallen at his command post in the Reich Chancellery fighting to the last breath against Bolshevism and for Germany". The Soviet flag is raised over the Reich Chancellery, by order of Stalin. Up to 2,500 people die in a mass suicide in Demmin following the advance of the Red Army.
Start of three-year Pilbara strike of Indigenous Australians.

main.desc: Workers strike in the 1940s in Western Australia

events.text: Sicilian separatist Salvatore Giuliano and his gang fired into a crowd of May Day marchers near Piana degli Albanesi, Sicily, killing 11 and wounding 33.
Portella della Ginestra massacre against May Day celebrations in Sicily by the bandit and separatist leader Salvatore Giuliano where 11 persons are killed and 33 wounded.

main.desc: 1947 mass killing by Sicilian separatists in Sicily, Italy

events.text: Gwendolyn Brooks became the first African American to receive the Pulitzer Prize for Poetry.
A Vickers VC.1 Viking crashes while attempting to return to Blackbushe Airport in Yateley, killing 34.
Cold War: U-2 incident: Francis Gary Powers, in a Lockheed U-2 spyplane, is shot down over the Sverdlovsk Oblast, Soviet Union, sparking a diplomatic crisis.

main.desc: 1947–1991 geopolitical rivalry between US and USSR

events.text: Vietnam War: A student anti-war strike erupts in response to U.S. and South Vietnamese forces attacking Vietnamese communists in a Cambodian Campaign.
Argentine president Juan Perón expelled Montoneros from a demonstration in the Plaza de Mayo in Buenos Aires, forcing the group to become a clandestine organization.

links.t: Expulsion of Montoneros from Plaza de Mayo

events.text: Operation Black Buck: The Royal Air Force attacks the Argentine Air Force during the Falklands War.

main.desc: Series of British long-range airstrikes during the Falklands War

events.text: In Major League Baseball, Rickey Henderson broke the record for stolen bases on the same night that Nolan Ryan broke his own record for no-hitters.
Angolan Civil War: The MPLA and UNITA agree to the Bicesse Accords, which are formally signed on May 31 in Lisbon.
Sri Lankan President Ranasinghe Premadasa is assassinated in Colombo in a suicide bombing carried out by the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam.
Three-time Formula One champion Ayrton Senna is killed in an accident during the San Marino Grand Prix.

links.t: List of Formula One World Drivers' Champions

events.text: The Labour Party wins the 1997 General Election and Tony Blair is elected as Prime Minister.
The Horncastle boar's head (pictured), which probably once formed part of the crest of an Anglo-Saxon helmet, was found.

Invasion of Iraq: In what becomes known as the "Mission Accomplished" speech, on board the USS Abraham Lincoln (off the coast of California), U.S. President George W. Bush declares that "major combat operations in Iraq have ended".

main.desc: Military invasion led by the United States

events.text: Cyprus, Czech Republic, Estonia, Hungary, Latvia, Lithuania, Malta, Poland, Slovakia, and Slovenia join the European Union, celebrated at the residence of the Irish President in Dublin.

main.desc: Island country in the Mediterranean Sea

events.text: Same-sex marriage in Sweden is legalized.
Faisal Shahzad attempted to detonate a car bomb in Times Square, New York City, but it failed to explode.
Faisal Shahzad attempts to detonate a car bomb in Times Square, but the bomb fails to go off.
Pope John Paul II is beatified by his successor, Pope Benedict XVI.

main.t: Beatification of Pope John Paul II

events.text: The evacuation of nearly 88,000 people began when a wildfire swept through Fort McMurray, Alberta, Canada, and burned for another 14 months, becoming the costliest disaster in Canadian history.
Syrian civil war: The Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF) resumes the Deir ez-Zor campaign in order to clear the remnants of the Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant (ISIL) from the Iraq–Syria border.
Naxalite attack in Gadchiroli district of India: Sixteen army soldiers, including a driver, killed in an IED blast. Naxals targeted an anti-Naxal operations team.
Naruhito ascends to the throne of Japan succeeding his father Akihito, beginning the Reiwa period.
The 2024 Loblaw boycott, a Canadian boycott against retail corporation and grocer Loblaw Companies, begins.
After a ransomware attack by the group ShinyHunters, the education platform Canvas operated by private company Instructure, goes offline, affecting thousands of educational institutions.
King Richard I of England gave the city of Portsmouth its first royal charter.
King Richard I of England gives Portsmouth its first royal charter.
William de Braose is hanged by Prince Llywelyn the Great.
Mamluks under Baybars murder the Ayyubid sultan Turanshah for fear of losing their privileges.

main.desc: Slave-soldiers and enslaved mercenaries in the Muslim world

events.text: The surrender of the Acropolis of Athens to Nerio Acciaioli ends the Catalan presence in the Duchy of Athens.

main.desc: Ancient citadel above the city of Athens

events.text: Anne Boleyn, Queen of England, is arrested and imprisoned on charges of adultery, incest, treason and witchcraft.
Presbyterian clergyman John Knox returned from exile to lead the Scottish Reformation.
John Knox returns from exile to Scotland to become the leader of the nascent Scottish Reformation.
Mary, Queen of Scots, escapes from Lochleven Castle.
The King James Version of the Bible is published for the first time in London, England, by printer Robert Barker.
Afonso Mendes, appointed by Pope Gregory XV as Latin Patriarch of Ethiopia, arrives at Beilul from Goa.

main.desc: Portuguese Jesuit theologian; Patriarch of Ethiopia from 1622 to 1634

events.text: A royal charter granted the Hudson's Bay Company a monopoly in the fur trade in Rupert's Land (present-day Canada).

main.desc: Document granting rights from a monarch

events.text: King Charles II of England grants a permanent charter to the Hudson's Bay Company to open up the fur trade in North America.

main.desc: King of England, Scotland, and Ireland from 1660 to 1685

events.text: Outbreak of the Peninsular War: The people of Madrid rise up in rebellion against French occupation. Francisco de Goya later memorializes this event in his painting The Second of May 1808.
The Siege of Cuautla during the Mexican War of Independence ends with both sides claiming victory.

main.desc: 1812 battle of the Mexican War of Independence

events.text: After anchoring nearby, Captain Charles Fremantle of HMS Challenger declares the Swan River Colony in Australia.
American Civil War: Stonewall Jackson is wounded by friendly fire while returning to camp after reconnoitering during the Battle of Chancellorsville. He succumbs to pneumonia eight days later.
Peruvian defenders fight off the Spanish fleet at the Battle of Callao.
Albert Günther publishes the first study to recognise that the New Zealand tuatara is not a lizard.
The April Uprising breaks out in Ottoman Bulgaria.
A dust explosion (depicted) at the world's largest flour mill in Minneapolis resulted in 18 deaths.

main.desc: Flour dust explosion in a Minneapolis mill in 1878

events.text: Cree and Assiniboine warriors win the Battle of Cut Knife, their largest victory over Canadian forces during the North-West Rebellion.
The Treaty of Wuchale was signed, ending the Italo-Ethiopian War, but differences in translation later led to another war.

main.desc: 1889 trade agreement between the Ethiopian Empire and the Kingdom of Italy

events.text: Menelik II, Emperor of Ethiopia, signs the Treaty of Wuchale, giving Italy control over Eritrea.
Closing ceremony of the Intercalated Games in Athens, Greece.
The first game of the Negro National League baseball is played in Indianapolis.
Germany's independent labor unions are replaced by the German Labour Front.
World War II: Following the coup d'état against Iraq Crown Prince 'Abd al-Ilah earlier that year, the United Kingdom launches the Anglo-Iraqi War to restore him to power.
World War II: General Helmuth Weidling, the German commander of Berlin, surrendered to Soviet forces led by Marshal Georgy Zhukov, ending the Battle of Berlin.
World War II: The Soviet Union announces the fall of Berlin.
World War II: The surrender of Caserta comes into effect, by which German troops in Italy cease fighting.

main.desc: German and Italian Fascist surrender document during WWII

events.text: World War II: The US 82nd Airborne Division liberates Wöbbelin concentration camp finding 1,000 dead prisoners, most of whom starved to death.

main.desc: Nazi concentration camp in Ludwigslust, Germany

events.text: World War II: A death march from Dachau to the Austrian border is halted by the segregated, all-Nisei 522nd Field Artillery Battalion of the U.S. Army in southern Bavaria, saving several hundred prisoners.
A De Havilland Comet makes the first jetliner flight with fare-paying passengers, from London to Johannesburg.
Berthold Seliger launches a rocket with three stages and a maximum flight altitude of more than 100 kilometres (62 mi) near Cuxhaven. It is the only sounding rocket developed in Germany.

main.desc: Defunct German aeronautical research & development company (1961–64)

events.text: Vietnam War: An explosion attributed to Viet Cong commandos caused the escort carrier USNS Card to sink in the port of Saigon.

Vietnam War: An explosion sinks the American aircraft carrier USNS Card while it is docked at Saigon. Two Viet Cong combat swimmers had placed explosives on the ship's hull. She is raised and returned to service less than seven months later.
First ascent of Shishapangma, the fourteenth highest mountain in the world and the lowest of the Eight-thousanders.
The British ocean liner Queen Elizabeth 2 departs on her maiden voyage to New York City.
ALM Flight 980 ditches in the Caribbean Sea near Saint Croix, killing 23.

main.desc: Aviation accident in the Caribbean Sea on 2 May 1970

events.text: In the early morning hours a fire breaks out at the Sunshine Mine located between Kellogg and Wallace, Idaho, killing 91 workers.

main.desc: Silver mine in Silver Valley, Idaho

events.text: Falklands War: HMS Conqueror sank the Argentine cruiser General Belgrano (pictured), the only ship ever to have been deliberately sunk by a nuclear submarine in battle.
Falklands War: The British nuclear submarine HMS Conqueror sinks the Argentine cruiser ARA General Belgrano.
Henri Toivonen was killed in an accident while leading the Tour de Corse rally, resulting in FISA banning the popular Group B rally cars for the following season.
Chernobyl disaster: The City of Chernobyl is evacuated six days after the disaster.

main.desc: 1986 nuclear accident in the Soviet Union

events.text: Cold War: Hungary begins dismantling its border fence with Austria, which allows a number of East Germans to defect.

main.desc: 1947–1991 geopolitical rivalry between US and USSR

links.t: Removal of Hungary's border fence with Austria

events.text: Croatian War of Independence: Serb forces began rocket attacks on the Croatian capital Zagreb, killing 7 people and injuring around 200 others.
During the Croatian War of Independence, the Army of the Republic of Serb Krajina fires cluster bombs at Zagreb, killing seven and wounding over 175 civilians.
The European Central Bank is founded in Brussels in order to define and execute the European Union's monetary policy.
Mireya Moscoso (pictured) became the first woman to be elected President of Panama.

links.t: List of heads of state of Panama

events.text: Panamanian general election: Mireya Moscoso becomes the first woman to be elected President of Panama.

links.t: List of heads of state of Panama

events.text: President Bill Clinton announces that accurate GPS access would no longer be restricted to the United States military.

main.desc: President of the United States from 1993 to 2001

events.text: Cyclone Manou formed in the Indian Ocean; over the next two weeks it struck Madagascar and left more than 100,000 people homeless.
The Yelwa massacre concludes. It began on 4 February 2004 when armed Muslims killed 78 Christians at Yelwa, Nigeria. In response, about 630 Muslims were killed by Christians on May 2.
The Chaitén volcano in Chile began to erupt for the first time since around 1640.

main.desc: Active volcano in Los Lagos Region, Chile

events.text: Cyclone Nargis makes landfall in Burma killing over 138,000 people and leaving millions of people homeless.
Chaitén Volcano begins erupting in Chile, forcing the evacuation of more than 4,500 people.

main.desc: Active volcano in Los Lagos Region, Chile

events.text: The Conservative Party of Canada won enough seats in the federal election to establish their first majority government.
Osama bin Laden was killed by U.S. Navy SEAL Team Six in his private residential compound in Abbottabad, Pakistan.

main.desc: 2011 U.S. military operation in Abbottabad, Pakistan

links.t: Osama bin Laden's compound in Abbottabad

events.text: Osama bin Laden, the mastermind behind the September 11 attacks and the FBI's most wanted fugitive, is killed by the United States Navy SEALs in Abbottabad, Pakistan.
An E. coli outbreak strikes Europe, mostly in Germany, leaving more than 30 people dead and many others are taken ill.
A pastel version of The Scream, by Norwegian painter Edvard Munch, sells for $120 million in a New York City auction, setting a new world record for a work of art at auction.
Russo-Ukrainian War: Forty-eight people were killed during a confrontation between pro-Russian protesters and pro-Ukrainian unity protesters in the southern Ukrainian port city of Odesa.
Two mudslides in Badakhshan Province, Afghanistan, killed at least 350 people.
Two mudslides in Badakhshan, Afghanistan, leave up to 2,500 people missing.
Mayan king Bird Jaguar IV of Yaxchilan in modern-day Chiapas, Mexico, assumes the throne.

main.desc: King of the ancient Mayan city of Yaxchilan from 752 to 768

events.text: German king Otto III chooses his cousin Bruno of Carinthia as pope following the death of Pope John XV. Bruno becomes pope under the name Gregory V.
The largest of a series of earthquakes struck the island of Rhodes, causing an estimated 30,000 casualties.
The largest of three earthquakes strikes the island of Rhodes and causes an estimated 30,000 casualties.
Nkuwu Nzinga, the ruler of the Kingdom of Kongo, was baptised as João I by Portuguese missionaries.

main.desc: 1390–1914 state in Central Africa; Portuguese vassal from 1857

events.text: Kongo monarch Nkuwu Nzinga is baptised by Portuguese missionaries, adopting the baptismal name of João I.

main.desc: 1390–1914 state in Central Africa; Portuguese vassal from 1857

events.text: Angered by the brutal onslaught of Spanish troops at Fort Caroline, a French force burns the San Mateo fort and massacres hundreds of Spaniards.

main.desc: Attempted French colonial settlement in Florida

events.text: The Treaty of Loudun was signed, ending a war that originally began as a power struggle for the French throne.
Treaty of Loudun ends a French civil war.
A total solar eclipse is visible across northern Europe and northern Asia, as predicted by Edmond Halley to within four minutes accuracy.
The Great Sejm of the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth ratified the first codified national constitution in Europe.
The Constitution of May 3 (the first modern constitution in Europe) is proclaimed by the Sejm of Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth.

Washington, D.C. is incorporated as a city after Congress abolishes the Board of Commissioners, the District's founding government. The "City of Washington" is given a mayor-council form of government.

main.desc: Federal capital district of the United States

events.text: Finnish War: Sweden loses the fortress of Sveaborg to Russia.
Peninsular War: The Madrid rebels who rose up on May 2 are executed near Príncipe Pío hill.

The Anglo-Portuguese army under Lord Wellington tries to halt a larger French army under Marshal Masséna marching to relieve Almeida in the Battle of Fuentes de Oñoro. After intense fighting, the French are repulsed.
Neapolitan War: Joachim Murat, King of Naples, is defeated by the Austrians at the Battle of Tolentino, the decisive engagement of the war.

main.desc: Conflict between the Kingdom of Naples and the Austrian Empire in 1815

events.text: The Canterbury and Whitstable Railway is opened; it is the first steam-hauled passenger railway to issue season tickets and include a tunnel.

main.desc: Early British railway line, opened in 1830

events.text: The University of Athens is founded in Athens, Greece.

main.t: National and Kapodistrian University of Athens

events.text: A long-running feud between two towns in Wisconsin came to a head when a schooner crashed into a bridge; they later merged to form the city of Milwaukee.
Thomas Bateman excavated a high-status barrow, discovering objects including the boar-crested Benty Grange helmet, and the Benty Grange hanging bowl
The boar-crested Anglo-Saxon Benty Grange helmet is discovered in a barrow on the Benty Grange farm in Derbyshire.

main.desc: Early medieval cultural group in Britain

events.text: The May Uprising in Dresden begins: The last of the German revolutions of 1848–49.

main.desc: 1849 failed revolution in Dresden, Kingdom of Saxony

events.text: A group of American mercenaries led by William Walker set sail from San Francisco to conquer Nicaragua.
American adventurer William Walker departs from San Francisco with about 60 men to conquer Nicaragua.

main.desc: American physician, lawyer, journalist, and mercenary (1824–1860)

events.text: The Great Fire of 1901 begins in Jacksonville, Florida.

main.desc: Fire that destroyed downtown Jacksonville, Florida

events.text: Edith Maryon's statuette The Dance of Anitra (pictured), one of the few of her works known to survive in private hands, was exhibited at the Royal Academy of Arts.
Raja Harishchandra, the first Indian feature-length film, was released.
Raja Harishchandra, the first full-length Indian feature film, is released, marking the beginning of the Indian film industry.
The oldest Royal Air Force station in continuous operation, RAF Northolt, opened as home to No. 4 Reserve Aeroplane Squadron.

main.desc: Air and space warfare force of the United Kingdom

events.text: Russian Civil War: Relying on Red Army troops in neighboring Azerbaijan, the Bolsheviks attempted to stage a coup d'etat in Georgia.

main.desc: Multi-party war in the former Russian Empire (1917–1922)

events.text: A Bolshevik coup fails in the Democratic Republic of Georgia.

main.desc: Failed Bolshevik coup in the Democratic Republic of Georgia

events.text: Under the British Government of Ireland Act, Ireland was partitioned into two self-governing territories, Northern and Southern Ireland.

main.desc: Act of the Parliament of the United Kingdom

events.text: Ireland is partitioned under British law by the Government of Ireland Act 1920, creating Northern Ireland and Southern Ireland.

main.desc: 1921 division of Ireland into two jurisdictions

events.text: West Virginia becomes the first state to legislate a broad sales tax, but does not implement it until a number of years later due to enforcement issues.

The Jinan incident begins with the deaths of twelve Japanese civilians by Chinese forces in Jinan, China, which leads to Japanese retaliation and the deaths of over 2,000 Chinese civilians in the following days.
Subhas Chandra Bose formed the All India Forward Bloc, a faction within the Indian National Congress, in opposition to Gandhi's tactics of nonviolence.
The All India Forward Bloc is formed by Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose.

Second World War: Japanese forces began an invasion of Tulagi and nearby islands in the British Solomon Islands, enabling them to threaten and intercept supply and communication routes between the United States and Australasia.

World War II: Japanese naval troops invade Tulagi Island in the Solomon Islands during the first part of Operation Mo that results in the Battle of the Coral Sea between Japanese forces and forces from the United States and Australia.
Second World War: The German ocean liner Cap Arcona, afloat in the Bay of Lübeck with thousands of concentration camp survivors on board, was attacked and sunk by the Royal Air Force.
World War II: Sinking of the prison ships Cap Arcona, Thielbek and Deutschland by the Royal Air Force in  Lübeck Bay, resulting in more than 7,000 deaths.

main.desc: Ship converted for use as a detention center

events.text: A new Constitution of Japan went into effect, providing for a parliamentary system of government, guaranteeing certain fundamental rights, and relegating the Japanese monarchy to a purely ceremonial role.
New post-war Japanese constitution goes into effect.
The U.S. Supreme Court rules in Shelley v. Kraemer that covenants prohibiting the sale of real estate to blacks and other minorities are legally unenforceable.

main.t: Supreme Court of the United States
main.desc: Highest court of jurisdiction in the U.S.

events.text: London's Royal Festival Hall opens with the Festival of Britain.

main.desc: Multi-purpose venue in the city of London, England

events.text: The United States Senate Committee on Armed Services and United States Senate Committee on Foreign Relations begin their closed door hearings into the relief of Douglas MacArthur by U.S. President Harry Truman.

main.t: United States Senate Committee on Armed Services
main.desc: Committee of the United States Senate

links.t: United States Senate Committee on Foreign Relations

events.text: Lieutenant Colonels Joseph O. Fletcher and William P. Benedict of the United States land a plane at the North Pole.
The Kentucky Derby is televised nationally for the first time, on the CBS network.

main.desc: American stakes race for Thoroughbreds, part of the Triple Crown

events.text: Two men are rescued from a semitrailer that crashed over the side of the Pit River Bridge before it fell into the Sacramento River. Amateur photographer Virginia Schau photographs "Rescue on Pit River Bridge", the first and only winning submission for the Pulitzer Prize for Photography to have been taken by a woman.

main.desc: Trailer vehicle without a front axle

events.text: Walter O'Malley, the owner of the Brooklyn Dodgers, agrees to move the team from Brooklyn to Los Angeles.
The Off-Broadway show The Fantasticks premiered, eventually becoming the world's longest-running musical, with 17,162 performances across 42 years.

main.desc: Type of theatre in New York City

events.text: Police in Birmingham, Alabama, used high-pressure water hoses and dogs against civil-rights protesters, bringing scrutiny on racial segregation in the southern United States.

links.t: Racial segregation in the United States

events.text: The police force in Birmingham, Alabama switches tactics and responds with violent force to stop the "Birmingham campaign" protesters. Images of the violent suppression are transmitted worldwide, bringing new-found attention to the civil rights movement.
Eighty-five people are killed when Braniff International Airways Flight 352 crashes near Dawson, Texas.
Erich Honecker became First Secretary of the Socialist Unity Party of Germany, the governing party of East Germany.
Erich Honecker becomes First Secretary of the Socialist Unity Party of Germany, remaining in power until 1989.

links.t: List of political office-holders in East Germany

events.text: The first unsolicited bulk commercial email (which would later become known as "spam") is sent by a Digital Equipment Corporation marketing representative to every ARPANET address on the west coast of the United States.
The Conservative Party wins the United Kingdom general election. The following day, Margaret Thatcher becomes the first female British Prime Minister.

links.t: Prime Minister of the United Kingdom

events.text: Twenty-one people are killed and forty-one are injured after a bomb explodes on Air Lanka Flight 512 at Colombo airport in Sri Lanka.

A crash by Bobby Allison at the Talladega Superspeedway, Alabama fencing at the start-finish line would lead NASCAR to develop the restrictor plate for the following season both at Daytona International Speedway and Talladega.
The Kargil War initiates when Indian forces detected the infiltration of Pakistani forces in Indian-administered Kargil, a city in Jammu and Kashmir.
A Doppler on Wheels team measured the fastest winds recorded on Earth, at 143.6 m/s (321 mph; 517 km/h), in a tornado near Bridge Creek, Oklahoma.

The southwestern portion of Oklahoma City is devastated by an F5 tornado, killing forty-five people, injuring 665, and causing $1 billion in damage. The tornado is one of 66 from the 1999 Oklahoma tornado outbreak. This tornado also produces the highest wind speed ever recorded, measured at 484 ± 32 kilometres per hour (301 ± 20 mph). In meteorology, the term "May 3" is synonymous with the F5 tornado.

main.desc: Capital city of Oklahoma, United States

events.text: Infiltration of Pakistani soldiers on Indian side results in the Kargil War.
The sport of geocaching begins, with the first cache placed and the coordinates from a GPS posted on Usenet.
The United States loses its seat on the U.N. Human Rights Commission for the first time since the commission was formed in 1947.

main.t: United Nations Commission on Human Rights
main.desc: Defunct functional commission of the United Nations

events.text: Armavia Flight 967 crashes into the Black Sea near Sochi International Airport in Sochi, Russia, killing 113 people.

main.desc: 2006 aviation accident in the Black Sea

events.text: Three-year-old British girl Madeleine McCann disappeared from a holiday apartment in Praia da Luz, Portugal; she has never been found.
The three-year-old British girl Madeleine McCann disappears in Praia da Luz, Portugal, starting "the most heavily reported missing-person case in modern history".
Two gunmen launch an attempted attack on an anti-Islam event in Garland, Texas, which was held in response to the Charlie Hebdo shooting.

main.desc: Failed terrorist attack in Texas, U.S.

Santiago de Vera becomes sixth governor-general of the Spanish colony of the Philippines.

main.desc: Army of the United States from 1775 to 1784

main.desc: 1834 final battle of the Portuguese Civil War

main.desc: Head of the Catholic Church from 1914 to 1922

The Tritons' Fountain in Valletta, Malta is turned on for the first time.
American physicist Theodore Maiman operated the first working laser at Hughes Research Laboratories in Malibu.
Theodore Maiman operates the first optical laser (a ruby laser), at Hughes Research Laboratories in Malibu, California.

Alan Turing submits On Computable Numbers for publication.
The rise of Neville Chamberlain culminated with his accession as Prime Minister of the United Kingdom, being summoned to Buckingham Palace to "kiss hands".

links.t: Prime Minister of the United Kingdom

Daniel François Malan is elected as Prime Minister of South Africa. He later goes on to implement Apartheid.

The Palestine Liberation Organization (PLO) is founded, with Yasser Arafat elected as its first leader.

Fifteen West African countries sign the Treaty of Lagos, creating the Economic Community of West African States.

main.desc: Westernmost region of the African continent

Konstantinos Karamanlis signs the full treaty of the accession of Greece with the European Economic Community.

links.t: British nuclear weapons and the Falklands War

U.S. President Bill Clinton's former business partners in the Whitewater land deal, Jim McDougal and Susan McDougal, and the Governor of Arkansas, Jim Guy Tucker, are convicted of fraud.

main.desc: President of the United States from 1993 to 2001

main.desc: Governing body of association football in England

links.t: Relocation of Wimbledon F.C. to Milton Keynes

The Iraqi Governing Council chooses Ayad Allawi, a longtime anti-Saddam Hussein exile, as prime minister of Iraq's interim government.

Malta votes on the introduction of divorce; the proposal was approved by 53% of voters, resulting in a law allowing divorce under certain conditions being enacted later in the year.
The Arkankergen massacre in Kazakhstan's Alakol District kills 15 people.

main.desc: 2012 attack in Kazakhstan on the border with China

The Roman emperor Julian defeats the Sasanian army in the Battle of Ctesiphon, under the walls of the Sasanian capital, but is unable to take the city.
A catastrophic earthquake hits Antioch, killing several thousands including patriarch Euphrasius.

main.desc: Earthquake striking Syria and Antioch in 526

events.text: Election of pope Paul I following the death of pope Stephen II in the previous month.

main.desc: Part of the Reconquista in present day Spain

main.desc: 1167 battle between the Holy Roman Empire and the Commune of Rome

main.desc: 1416 Naval battle between the Republic of Venice and the Ottoman Empire

main.desc: 1453 Ottoman conquest of the Byzantine capital

main.desc: 1660 restoration of the monarchy in the British Isles

Swedish operatic soprano Jenny Lind concluded a successful concert tour of the United States under the management of showman P. T. Barnum.

The Hong Kong General Chamber of Commerce is founded, in Hong Kong.

The pharmacist John Pemberton places his first advertisement for Coca-Cola, which appeared in The Atlanta Journal.

Igor Stravinsky's ballet score The Rite of Spring receives its premiere performance in Paris, France, provoking a near-riot.
The ocean liner RMS Empress of Ireland sinks in the Gulf of Saint Lawrence with the loss of 1,012 lives.

Armenia defeats the Ottoman Army in the Battle of Sardarabad.

links.t: Andrew Claude de la Cherois Crommelin

Michele Schirru, a citizen of the United States, is executed by a Royal Italian Army firing squad for intent to kill Benito Mussolini.
World War I veterans begin to assemble in Washington, D.C., in the Bonus Army to request cash bonuses promised to them to be paid in 1945.
A strike by copper miners in Northern Rhodesia ended after six workers were shot and killed by police.
First flight of the Messerschmitt Bf 109 fighter aeroplane.
Bing Crosby recorded his version of the song "White Christmas", which went on to become the best-selling single worldwide, with more than 50 million copies sold.
First combat mission of the Consolidated B-32 Dominator heavy bomber.
United Airlines Flight 521 crashes at LaGuardia Airport, killing 43.

main.desc: 1947 aviation accident over the United States

main.desc: UN peacekeeping mission in the Middle East

Diane Leather became the first woman to run a mile in less than five minutes.
Chinese police open fire on protesters in Yining, Xinjiang, killing at least five people and wounding a dozen others.

main.desc: 1962 mass exodus of people from China to the Soviet Union

SETA, a Finnish LGBT rights organisation, is founded in Helsinki.

main.desc: Head of the Catholic Church from 1978 to 2005

main.desc: Fatal spectator riot in Brussels, Belgium in 1985

Space Shuttle Discovery completes the first docking with the International Space Station.

Cold War: Spain joins NATO.

events.text: 53 people are killed in a stampede at the Nyamiha metro station in Minsk, Belarus.

main.desc: 2003 mob violence against the National League for Democracy in Sagaing Division, Myanmar

events.text: American student Natalee Holloway disappeared on a high-school graduation trip to Aruba.

main.desc: 2005 disappearance of an American in Aruba

Convention on Cluster Munitions is adopted.
TACA Flight 390 overshoots the runway at Toncontín International Airport in Tegucigalpa, Honduras and crashes, killing five people.

events.text: Petronius Maximus, the ruler of the Western Roman Empire, was stoned to death by a mob as he fled Rome before Vandal forces arrived and sacked the city.
Emperor Petronius Maximus is stoned to death by an angry mob while fleeing Rome.
A Mongol army under Genghis Khan captured Zhongdu (modern Beijing), the capital of the Jin dynasty of China.
Zhongdu (now Beijing), then under the control of the Jurchen ruler Emperor Xuanzong of Jin, is captured by the Mongols under Genghis Khan, ending the Battle of Zhongdu.
Mongol invasion of Kievan Rus': Mongol forces defeated a Kievan Rus' army at the Battle of the Kalka River in present-day Ukraine.

Mongols depart Java after the failed Mongol invasion against King Kertanegara of Singhasari.
Cardinal Bessarion announced his donation of 746 Greek and Latin codices to the Republic of Venice, forming the Biblioteca Marciana.
King Henry III lays the first stone of the Pont Neuf (New Bridge), the oldest bridge of Paris, France.
The pageant London's Love to Prince Henry on the River Thames celebrates the creation of Prince Henry as Prince of Wales.
Citing poor eyesight as a reason, Samuel Pepys records the last event in his diary.

American Revolution: The Committee of Safety of Mecklenburg County, North Carolina, adopted the Mecklenburg Resolves, which annulled and vacated all laws originating from the authority of the king or the Parliament of Great Britain.
American Revolution: The Mecklenburg Resolves are adopted in the Province of North Carolina.
Manuel Quimper explores the Strait of Juan de Fuca.
The United States enacts its first copyright statute, the Copyright Act of 1790.

main.t: Copyright law of the United States

events.text: French Revolution: The Revolutionary Tribunal is suppressed.
French and Spanish forces begin the assault against British forces occupying Diamond Rock, Martinique.

main.desc: 1805 battle of the War of the Third Coalition

events.text: In Australia, William Lawson, Gregory Blaxland and William Wentworth reach Mount Blaxland, effectively marking the end of a route across the Blue Mountains.

main.desc: English born Australian explorer and politician (1774–1850)

events.text: Qajar Iran and the Ottoman Empire determine their international boundary in the second treaty of Erzurum.
The Great Clock at the Houses of Parliament (now known as the Elizabeth Tower) starts keeping time.
American Civil War: Confederate troops under Joseph E. Johnston and G. W. Smith engaged Union forces under George B. McClellan at the Battle of Seven Pines outside Richmond, Virginia.
American Civil War: Peninsula Campaign: Confederate forces under Joseph E. Johnston and G.W. Smith engage Union forces under George B. McClellan outside the Confederate capital of Richmond, Virginia.

main.desc: 1864 series of battles in Virginia during the American Civil War

main.desc: Former arena in Manhattan, New York

events.text: The arrival at Plymouth of Tāwhiao, King of Maoris, to claim the protection of Queen Victoria.

main.desc: City and unitary authority in Devon, England

events.text: Johnstown Flood: Over 2,200 people die after a dam fails and sends a 60-foot (18-meter) wall of water over the town of Johnstown, Pennsylvania.
The Second Boer War came to an end with the signing of the Treaty of Vereeniging in Pretoria, South Africa.
Second Boer War: The Treaty of Vereeniging ends the war and ensures British control of South Africa.
The attempted regicide of Spanish King Alfonso XIII and Queen Victoria Eugenie on their wedding day instead kills 24.

main.desc: 1906 attempted murder of King Alfonso XIII and Victoria Eugenie

links.t: Wedding of Alfonso XIII and Princess Victoria Eugenie

main.desc: Constitution of the Union of South Africa (1910–1961)

events.text: The RMS Titanic is launched in Belfast, Northern Ireland.

main.desc: British passenger liner that sank in 1912

events.text: The President of Mexico Porfirio Díaz flees the country during the Mexican Revolution.
World War I: Battle of Jutland: The British Grand Fleet engages the High Seas Fleet in the largest naval battle of the war, which proves indecisive.
The Tulsa race massacre kills at least 39, but other estimates of black fatalities vary from 55 to about 300.
Hope Development School fire kills 24 people, mostly disabled children.
A magnitude-7.7 earthquake struck Balochistan in British India, now part of Pakistan, killing between 30,000 and 60,000 people
A 7.7 Mw earthquake destroys Quetta in modern-day Pakistan killing 40,000.
World War II: German forces dropped four bombs on neutral Ireland, killing 28 people and damaging Áras an Uachtaráin, the residence of the President of Ireland.

links.t: Bombing of Dublin in World War II

events.text: Anglo-Iraqi War: The United Kingdom completes the re-occupation of Iraq and returns 'Abd al-Ilah to power as regent for Faisal II.
World War II: Imperial Japanese Navy midget submarines begin a series of attacks on Sydney, Australia.

Ferenc Nagy, the democratically elected Prime Minister of Hungary, resigns from office after blackmail from the Hungarian Communist Party accusing him of being part of a plot against the state. This grants the Communists effective control of the Hungarian government.
The Uniform Code of Military Justice takes effect as the legal system of the United States Armed Forces.
The U.S. Supreme Court expands on its Brown v. Board of Education decision by ordering district courts and school districts to enforce educational desegregation "at all deliberate speed."

main.desc: Fundamental law of South Africa from 1961 to 1984

events.text: In Moscow City Court, the Rokotov–Faibishenko show trial begins, despite the Khrushchev Thaw to reverse Stalinist elements in Soviet society.
The West Indies Federation dissolves.

main.desc: 1958–1962 political union of British island colonies in the Caribbean

events.text: The 7.9 Mw Ancash earthquake shakes Peru with a maximum Mercalli intensity of VIII (Severe) and a landslide buries the town of Yungay, Peru. Between 66,794 and 70,000 were killed and 50,000 were injured.

main.desc: Earthquake and resulting avalanche in Peru

main.desc: 1968 United States law regarding federal holidays

main.desc: Upper house of the US Congress

events.text: Indian Airlines Flight 440 crashes near Palam Airport in Delhi, killing 48.
The Trans-Alaska Pipeline System is completed.

An organized mob of police and government-sponsored Sinhalese paramilitary forces began three days of attacks that led to the burning of the Jaffna Public Library (renovated building pictured) in Sri Lanka, destroying more than 97,000 items in one of the most violent 20th-century examples of ethnic biblioclasm.

The Ariane 2 rocket is launched on its maiden flight, carrying Intelsat VA F-14, but the mission ends in failure.
Bicesse Accords in Angola lay out a transition to multi-party democracy under the supervision of the United Nations' UNAVEM II peacekeeping mission.

main.desc: 1991 agreement to transition to democracy in Angola

links.t: United Nations Angola Verification Mission II

events.text: The Confederation Bridge opens, linking Prince Edward Island with mainland New Brunswick.

main.desc: Canadian bridge from Prince Edward Island to the mainland

events.text: Air France retires its fleet of Concorde aircraft.
Vanity Fair reveals that Mark Felt was "Deep Throat".
Usain Bolt breaks the world record in the 100m sprint, with a wind-legal (+1.7 m/s) 9.72 seconds.
Space Shuttle Discovery launches on STS-124 carrying the second portion of the Japanese Kibō module to the International Space Station.
American physician George Tiller, one of the few doctors in the country who performed late-term abortions, was shot and killed by Scott Roeder, an anti-abortion activist.

Israeli Shayetet 13 commandos board the Gaza Freedom Flotilla while still in international waters trying to break the ongoing blockade of the Gaza Strip; nine Turkish citizens on the flotilla were killed in the ensuing violent affray.

main.desc: Special operations unit of the Israeli Navy

The asteroid 1998 QE2 and its moon make their closest approach to Earth for the next two centuries.
